subtype: Approach: groupthink over an unaffordable plan [Pitfall]
passage: Thursday night, hostel. Today the group locked the beach plan and everyone said "sounds great". So did I. The total per head is far above what my monthly allowance can carry, and I kept telling myself I'd manage. I could not bring myself to call it too much when the others looked so pleased. Deposit was due at four and I skipped canteen lunches all week to make it. I told Bhavna I had a headache when they went for dinner, because I could not pay for that as well. Tonight the chat is full of packing lists and I feel outside it, like a guest at my own trip. I should have spoken on Monday. Signed, Harsha.

qa.q: What did Harsha skip all week to make the deposit?
qa.a: Harsha skipped canteen lunches all week to make the deposit.

qa.q: What was Harsha feeling when joining in with "sounds great"?
qa.a: Harsha felt awkward and afraid of spoiling everyone's excitement, so Harsha stayed quiet about the cost.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Harsha have used, and why?
qa.a: Harsha could have asked privately for a cheaper option before the group locked the plan, because a quiet word is easier than speaking up in front of everyone.

qa.q: How might Bhavna see the headache excuse?
qa.a: Bhavna may have believed the excuse and not guessed the money problem, which means the group missed the chance to change the plan.

grounding: A member with a tight allowance stays silent about a costly plan, then struggles to pay and feels left out.

subtype: Approach: groupthink over an unaffordable plan [Pitfall]

Karthik: you ok? you were quiet at dinner
Sunaina: yeah just tired
Karthik: you sure? you said yes to the goa resort really fast last month
Sunaina: everyone else said yes. I didn't want to be the one who kills the plan
Sunaina: it's 9,000 for three nights. my monthly allowance is 6,000
Karthik: oh. why didn't you say anything?
Sunaina: say what? 'sorry, I'm the broke one'?
Sunaina: I've been cutting back on everything for weeks. and tonight when they ordered the seafood platter I said I wasn't hungry
Karthik: sunaina, I think at least two others were stretching too. nobody wanted to say it
Sunaina: great. so we're all pretending
Sunaina: I feel so left out on a trip I'm literally on 😔

qa.q: Why did Sunaina say yes so fast, and how does it feel now?
qa.a: Sunaina didn't want to be the one to kill the plan, and now feels left out and ashamed of having to pretend.

qa.q: What could the group have done when choosing the resort?
qa.a: Ask everyone to share a comfortable price range privately, so the plan fits the tightest budget without anyone being singled out.

qa.q: What does Karthik suspect about the rest of the group?
qa.a: Karthik suspects at least two others were stretching too, which shows the silence hurt more than one person.

grounding: Shows a friend on a tight allowance agreeing silently to a costly plan so as not to be the odd one out, then struggling and feeling excluded.

subtype: Approach: groupthink over an unaffordable plan [Pitfall]
passage:
At the bus stand tea shop in Mandya, the six friends from the agricultural college voted on the trip in two minutes. Shalini had found a resort in Ooty with a heated pool: 4,500 each for two nights. 'Everyone okay?' she asked. Five hands went up quickly. Harish's went up last.
Harish's father sent him 3,000 a month from the sugarcane money, and most of it went on the hostel mess. He did the maths under the table and felt his stomach sink. But everyone else had said yes, and he didn't want to be the one who spoiled it.
He borrowed from his cousin, told no one, and on the trip said he was 'not a pool person'. While the others swam, he sat in the room scrolling his phone. At dinner they ordered dishes he didn't dare share.
On the bus back, Shalini noticed how quiet he was. He said he was tired.

qa.q: How much did the Ooty resort cost each?
What was Harish feeling when he raised his hand last?
qa.a: He felt his stomach sink, anxious about the cost, but afraid of spoiling the plan for everyone.

qa.q: What could Shalini have done differently when asking 'Everyone okay?'
qa.a: Offer two options at different prices and let people vote privately, so no one has to admit a tight budget in front of the group.

qa.q: How might the trip look to Shalini on the bus back?
qa.a: Shalini notices Harish is quiet but may not guess why, since he hid the cost and said he was only tired.

grounding: Shows a student with a tight allowance silently agreeing to a costly trip, borrowing to pay and feeling left out while the others enjoy it.
